title: Pre-Seed Finance Operations Playbook for Startups
summary: Pre-seed finance setup done right: entity choice, Delaware franchise tax, QSBS and 83(b) clocks, R&D docs, and a lean tooling stack. See where to start.
body_markdown:
## What Changes at Pre-Seed


Pre-seed finance setup means putting the smallest correct set of financial systems in place at incorporation, not at your first dollar of revenue. The moment you form an entity and open a business bank account, you become a separate legal taxpayer with filing obligations that exist whether or not you have customers. Pre-seed startup accounting isn’t about sophistication. It’s about a clean, boring foundation the next person to touch your books doesn’t have to rebuild.


Companies at this stage usually sit between pre-revenue and roughly $500K ARR, with one to five people and no formal investor reporting yet. You’re not running a finance department. You’re running a finance function of one, part-time, yourself. The startup accounting basics that matter here are narrow, and they’re worth doing well the first time.


What actually changes at incorporation isn’t the volume of transactions. It’s the arrival of obligations and clocks that didn’t exist the day before:


- **You become a filer.** A C-Corp must file Form 1120 for every year it exists, even with zero revenue and zero activity.
- **One-time tax clocks start.** The QSBS holding period and the 83(b) election window begin at stock issuance and can’t be restarted later.
- **Compliance clocks begin.** The Delaware franchise clock, the QSBS five-year hold, and R&D documentation all start now.
- **Bookkeeping becomes a monthly habit.** Cash-basis categorization and a clean chart of accounts, kept current, not reconstructed at diligence.


The trap is reading “we’re pre-revenue” as “we don’t need accounting.” A company with no sales still has a bank account, a set of formation costs, and a tax return waiting for it. The finance function starts at incorporation, not at first dollar. For the mechanics of standing up that first ledger, our guide to[startup accounting 101](https://www.indinero.com/blog/indinero-guide-to-startup-accounting-101/) walks through the foundation before you have a full month of transactions.


## Service Requirements


Three services cover the whole of pre-seed: bookkeeping, basic tax filing, and entity setup support. Everything else can wait. R&D credit studies and 409A valuations generally aren’t required yet, because there are usually no option grants and often no payroll to offset.

**Bookkeeping comes first, and cash basis is fine.** Categorize every transaction, reconcile the bank account monthly, and keep a clean chart of accounts. Cash basis is far simpler than accrual at this stage and perfectly acceptable. Seed-stage GAAP diligence will eventually push you to accrual, so the one thing to protect now is a clean chart of accounts that makes that conversion painless later.


**Tax filing is narrow but non-optional.** At minimum you owe a first federal Form 1120, your state-of-incorporation return, and the Delaware annual franchise report if you incorporated there. None of these depends on having revenue.


**Entity setup is cheap to do right and expensive to unwind.** Getting the incorporation, the founder stock issuance, the 83(b) elections, and the cap table correct the first time protects benefits you can’t recover later.


The first finance hire startup founders make is rarely at pre-seed. Founder-led finance plus outsourced bookkeeping is the norm until seed, and hiring a full-time controller before you have transactions to control is a common way to burn runway. A separate bank account, a clean chart of accounts, and basic monthly bookkeeping are usually all you need before a dedicated accounting firm makes sense.

Most firms price each of those separately, which means three vendors, three onboarding cycles, and three handoffs the day your books need to talk to your tax return.


## Compliance Triggers


Several compliance clocks switch on at incorporation, regardless of revenue. This is the section founders underestimate, because most of these obligations exist before you have a single customer.


1.


**Entity formation, the venture-track decision.** Nearly all venture firms require a Delaware C-Corp, because they need to issue preferred stock and can’t take on the pass-through tax exposure an LLC creates. If you plan to raise institutional capital within 12 to 18 months, incorporate as a[Delaware C-Corp](https://www.indinero.com/blog/delaware-incorporation-taxes/) from day one. Converting an LLC later carries cost, complexity, and potential tax friction. If you’re bootstrapping with no VC plans, an LLC’s pass-through simplicity can fit better.


2.


**Delaware franchise tax.** Every Delaware corporation owes an annual franchise tax and files an annual report by March 1. The state’s[franchise tax calculator](https://corp.delaware.gov/frtaxcalc/) puts the minimum at $175 under the Authorized Shares Method and $400 under the Assumed Par Value Capital Method, plus a $50 report fee, and you may use whichever method produces the lower bill. Startups often get a shocking five-figure default bill because Delaware assumes the Authorized Shares Method. Recalculating under Assumed Par Value, appropriate for a company with millions of authorized shares but few assets, usually drops it back to the minimum. If you also operate in California, our note on[Delaware startups and California compliance](https://www.indinero.com/blog/delaware-startups-california-compliance/) covers the second filing.


3.


**Your first Form 1120.** Due April 15 for calendar-year C-Corps, the 15th day of the fourth month after year-end. A mid-year incorporation creates a short first tax year, but the filing is still required. An automatic six-month extension is available via Form 7004, though it extends time to file, not time to pay.


4.


**The QSBS clock starts at issuance.** Founder stock in a C-Corp can qualify for the Qualified Small Business Stock gain exclusion under IRC Section 1202, and the holding-period clock starts once, at original issuance. Under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, for stock issued after July 4, 2025, the exclusion is now tiered: 50% at a three-year hold, 75% at four years, and the full 100% at five years. The AICPA’s The Tax Adviser[breaks down the new tiers](https://www.thetaxadviser.com/issues/2025/nov/qsbs-gets-a-makeover-what-tax-pros-need-to-know-about-sec-1202s-new-look/) , which also raised the per-issuer cap from $10 million to $15 million and the gross-assets ceiling from $50 million to $75 million. To preserve the benefit, keep your stock certificates, board resolutions, purchase agreements, the 83(b) election, and the balance sheets that document the gross-assets test. Founders should file the Section 83(b) election within 30 days of issuance. That window doesn’t reopen. For the mechanics, see our[QSBS exemption guide](https://www.indinero.com/blog/qsbs-exemption/) .


5.


**R&D credit eligibility begins with your first QRE.** You can’t claim yet with no payroll, but the documentation starts now. A qualified small business, meaning gross receipts under $5 million in the credit year and none more than five years back, can elect to apply up to $500,000 a year of the research credit against the employer Social Security portion of payroll tax, which the[IRS spells out](https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/qualified-small-business-payroll-tax-credit-for-increasing-research-activities) in its payroll-credit guidance. Separately, Section 174A now restores immediate expensing of domestic R&D costs for tax years beginning after December 31, 2024, as Grant Thornton’s analysis of the change confirms. Track qualified research expenses from day one so the credit is claimable the moment you have a team. Our[R&D tax credit guide](https://www.indinero.com/resources/rd-tax-credit-guide/) covers eligibility.


6.


**Sales-tax nexus monitoring starts in your home state.** After South Dakota v. Wayfair, states can impose sales-tax collection on remote sellers that cross an economic threshold, commonly $100,000 in sales or 200 transactions, though the[Sales Tax Institute](https://www.salestaxinstitute.com/sales_tax_faqs/wayfair-economic-nexus) notes the rules vary by state. Physical presence in your home state creates nexus immediately, so watch that first and monitor others as revenue grows. Many states tax SaaS differently, so taxability isn’t automatic. Our primer on[startup sales-tax nexus](https://www.indinero.com/blog/startup-tax-nexus/) explains where to watch.


## The Typical Tooling Stack


The pre-seed stack is lean and integrated: a general ledger, a bank account, a payment processor, and payroll only once you hire. The point isn’t the specific logos. It’s a bank and a payment processor that feed a single general ledger cleanly, so the monthly reconcile takes minutes, not a weekend.


Category Tool(s) Why


General ledger QuickBooks Online (or Xero) The system of record everything else feeds


Banking Mercury, Brex, or Ramp A startup-friendly account with a clean feed into the ledger


Revenue and payments Stripe Syncs collected revenue into the ledger


Payroll Gusto Added at your first hire, and what turns on your future R&D payroll offset


Add Gusto only when you make your first hire, because that’s also what turns on your future R&D payroll-credit offset. Until then, you don’t need it. Keep the stack small and keep the connections clean. Every tool you add before you need it is another integration to reconcile and another place for the numbers to drift.


The discipline that matters at pre-seed isn’t the toolset, it’s the wiring. When your bank account and payment processor both push into one ledger, categorization is a review task instead of a data-entry marathon. That’s the difference between a monthly close that takes an afternoon and a year-end that takes a week you don’t have.


Indinero integrates with your existing stack, with no proprietary platform lock-in. Your books live in QuickBooks or Xero and stay yours, so there’s no migration and no re-learning a platform if your needs change. That portability matters more than it looks at pre-seed, because the stack you set up now is the one a seed investor’s diligence team will open next year. Clean wiring today is clean diligence later.


## Common Mistakes at This Stage


Most pre-seed mistakes are one-time and permanent, which is what makes them expensive. Here are the five that cost founders the most.


1.


**Skipping bookkeeping entirely.** The single most expensive mistake. Founders who plan to “get to it later” arrive at seed diligence facing a 12-month reconstruction of a year they barely remember, during the exact weeks they should be selling the round. A little monthly discipline now, or a modest[bookkeeping engagement](https://www.indinero.com/services/online-bookkeeping-services/) , prevents all of it. The catch-up always costs more than the maintenance would have.


2.


**Forming an LLC when the plan is venture-track.** Comfortable now, costly later. If institutional money is the plan, the Delaware C-Corp belongs at day one, because converting an LLC later carries cost, complexity, and potential tax friction. The right time to decide is before you issue a single share, not the week your term sheet arrives.


3.


**Fumbling the QSBS and 83(b) paperwork.** Both are one-time, deadline-bound, and permanent if missed. The[83(b) election](https://www.indinero.com/blog/83b-startup-taxes/) window is 30 days from issuance. The QSBS clock never restarts. There’s no amended return that quietly fixes a missed election, so the paperwork you file in your first month can be worth more than any single deal you close in year one.


4.


**Treating cash basis as forever.** Cash basis is fine at pre-seed, but a messy chart of accounts makes the later GAAP-accrual conversion painful. The fix costs nothing now. Set the chart up clean, keep categories consistent, and the seed-stage switch to accrual is a formatting job, not a rebuild. For the underlying habits, our[bookkeeping basics for small business](https://www.indinero.com/blog/bookkeeping-basics-small-business/) covers the ground rules.


5.


**Ignoring the R&D credit until “later.”** With no contemporaneous documentation, you leave a payroll-tax offset worth up to $500,000 a year on the table once you have a team. The records cost nothing to keep now and a lot to reconstruct later. Track qualified research from your first engineering dollar, even before you have payroll to offset it against.


## What’s Coming Next: Seed-Stage Triggers


The pre-seed playbook ends the day your first priced round closes. That single event flips several switches at once and moves you into the Seed stage. Stage transitions stack.


Issuing preferred stock and granting employee options triggers the need for a 409A valuation to set a defensible strike price on every future grant. Investor reporting becomes real, with a board that expects a monthly or quarterly cadence and actuals it can trust. And diligence, both for this round and the next, expects GAAP-clean, often accrual-basis books. Multi-state sales-tax nexus monitoring also gets more real as revenue and customers spread across states.


The clean foundation you built at pre-seed is what makes the seed transition a formatting exercise instead of an emergency. The Seed-stage playbook picks up each of these in detail, and the overview hub for finance operations by funding stage maps the full sequence from pre-seed through public. The through-line is simple. The clean books you keep now become the first line of your post-seed bookkeeping checklist, so nothing has to be rebuilt when the money arrives.


For a broader view of how[outsourced accounting for startups](https://www.indinero.com/blog/outsourced-accounting-for-startups/) scales across these transitions, the mechanics are the same team taking on more scope as the requirements grow. That continuity is the whole reason to set the foundation correctly now, instead of discovering the gaps in a data room.

## Frequently asked questions


Common pre-seed finance questions, answered below. These cover what to set up first, when to incorporate and as what entity, and how the QSBS and bookkeeping decisions play out.


### What finance work actually matters at pre-seed?


At pre-seed, only three things matter: monthly bookkeeping, basic tax filing, and getting your entity and founder stock set up correctly. R&D credit studies, 409A valuations, and a fractional CFO can wait until you have payroll and option grants. Indinero’s Essential tier, with pricing that starts at $750/mo, bundles the bookkeeping, tax filing, and entity support that a pre-seed founder actually needs, then adds scope as real triggers appear.


### Does a pre-seed company need bookkeeping or just a shoebox of receipts?


A pre-seed company needs real monthly bookkeeping, not a shoebox of receipts, because clean books are what seed diligence opens first. Cash basis is fine at this stage, but categorize every transaction, reconcile the bank account monthly, and keep a clean chart of accounts. The alternative is a 12-month reconstruction during the exact weeks you should be raising. Indinero handles that monthly bookkeeping inside your existing QuickBooks or Xero, so nothing gets rebuilt later.


### When should a pre-seed founder incorporate, and as what entity?


A pre-seed founder planning to raise venture capital within 12 to 18 months should incorporate as a Delaware C-Corp from day one. Nearly all venture firms require a C-Corp so they can issue preferred stock, and converting an LLC later carries cost, complexity, and tax friction. If you’re bootstrapping with no VC plans, an LLC’s pass-through simplicity can fit better. Indinero supports both structures, so the entity decision matches the path you’re actually on.


### What is QSBS and why should pre-seed founders care?


QSBS, or Qualified Small Business Stock, lets founders exclude up to 100% of capital gains on C-Corp stock held long enough under IRC Section 1202. The holding-period clock starts once, at original issuance, and can’t be restarted, so pre-seed is when it begins. For stock issued after July 4, 2025, the exclusion is tiered: 50% at three years, 75% at four, and 100% at five. Indinero’s entity and QSBS-documentation support keeps the certificates and 83(b) records that protect the benefit.


### What is the cheapest finance setup that doesn’t create problems later?


The cheapest safe pre-seed finance setup is a separate business bank account, a clean chart of accounts, and basic monthly bookkeeping. Add a payment processor that feeds your general ledger, file your first Form 1120 and any Delaware franchise report, and get the 83(b) election filed within 30 days. Hiring a full-time controller before you have transactions to control just burns runway. Indinero’s Essential tier, with pricing that starts at $750/mo, covers this without three separate vendors.


### When does pre-seed become seed-stage from a finance perspective?


Pre-seed becomes seed-stage the day your first priced round closes, which triggers a 409A valuation, real investor reporting, and GAAP-clean books. Issuing preferred stock and granting employee options creates the need for a defensible strike price, and a board starts expecting monthly or quarterly actuals it can trust. Diligence also expects accrual-basis books. Indinero scales from monthly bookkeeping to your first 409A and fractional CFO support in the same engagement, with no handoff to a new firm.


### Can a pre-seed startup wait on bookkeeping until they raise their first round?


No, a pre-seed startup shouldn’t wait on bookkeeping, because deferring it turns seed diligence into a 12-month catch-up during your fundraise. The moment you incorporate and open a business bank account, you have formation costs, a tax return, and compliance clocks running whether or not you have revenue. Catch-up bookkeeping always costs more than the monthly maintenance would have. Indinero keeps the books current from month one, so the seed switch to accrual is a formatting job, not a rebuild.
